Good value dinner buffet
Feb 2018 • Couples
We pre booked the dinner buffet as we only had a 1 night stopover and didn't want to trek around outside trying to find somewhere reasonable. It turned out to be a reasonable choice and certainly good value. it was quiet when we went at the end of the Tet holiday in February with only half a dozen people or so there. 

A largish restaurant area, which is also the venue for breakfast, just off the main lobby and overlooking the pool. There was a good range of cold meat (including, sausages, hams, pates), fish and salady starters. there's also a good range of cheeses in the cold section. you could realistically just have these. The cold section is probably the jewel in the crown of the dinner buffet, as the hot section lets it down in quality, although the range, including crocodile when we went adds an exotic touch.There is a varied range of desserts, some home made, but perhaps a good idea if more were made in house. It was a shame that the Sea Bass on the live cooking station was cold and my wife mentioned this to the manager Ky, when he was doing his rounds, no great issue but it was worth pointing out.

Ky and his staff were friendly, attentive and efficient. Ky certainly knows how to do his job, with an extensive knowledge of food and wine, a credit and an asset to the F&B department.

Breakfast, buffet style was not the best we had experienced on previous visits to Ho Chi Minh. the range available was quite limited for a more high end hotel, but perhaps this was because the hotel was quiet - fair enough. A quick breakfast fro us as we had to leave for the airport but for those who like to linger over breakfast, which we do when there is time, perhaps on this occasion, it was because the hotel was quiet. worth a go for the dinner buffet though.

Good value for dinner buffet, but far away
Mar 2016 • Couples
The Garden Brasserie is the main restaurant at Park Royal hotel, an establishment not far away from the airport. 

I try to avoid buffet (since they lead to serious overeating) but I was invited for a celebratory dinner. 

This is a standard hotel buffet, with several "isles": salads, cheese and cold cuts, meat and seasfood, sushi and sashimi, desserts and the BBQ station. 

Things of note: some "weird" dishes available, such as frog legs, ostrich and even crocodile. Seafood and meat at the BBQ were not really great, just a few cuts available and only seabass and salmon. Toward the end the waiter announced that a lobster and foir gras were available, we joined the order. Not sure if this is standard practice or if it was a special treat. 

As compared to other five start buffet, variety was a bit limited, I would rate the food quality high. Sushi, sashimi and oysters were very fresh and reasonably tasty. The chicken with apricot was a special treat. 

Overall I liked it.

Only problem, at least for me, is the distance from district 1. If you travel by taxi, the extra distance can easily offset any saving for the slightly cheaper price as compared to other five star buffets.
